claude.finalText:
I changed the Coinbase endpoint URLs and two README links. I haven't run the bot, and I didn't test any of the new URLs, so please check them against your own API keys before trading with real money.

**What the repo uses:** the Coinbase Pro API (a REST and WebSocket trading API), through the deprecated `coinbase-pro` npm package and a hand-written client in `coinbaseProLibrary.js`. It also uses `axios`, `pino`, `dotenv` and the CSV libraries, and I found nothing affecting those.

**What changed:**
- Coinbase retired the Pro API and its `*.pro.coinbase.com` hosts. The API is now Coinbase Exchange, which is documented at docs.cdp.coinbase.com.
- The old URLs in the three strategy files are replaced with the Exchange ones. The sandbox URLs come from Coinbase's docs page. The production URLs, `https://api.exchange.coinbase.com` and `wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com`, I took from search results and Coinbase's naming pattern. I couldn't open the production runbook page to confirm them.

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Production REST | `https://api.pro.coinbase.com` | `https://api.exchange.coinbase.com` |
| Production WebSocket | `wss://ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com` | `wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com` |
| Sandbox REST | `https://api-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com` | `https://api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com` |
| Sandbox WebSocket | `wss://ws-feed-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com` | `wss://ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com` |

- The URLs are in `momentumTrading.js`, `momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js` and `reverseMomentumTrading.js`.
- In `README.md` I updated the sandbox and API docs links. The README still says "Coinbase Pro" in several places and links to the old `pro.coinbase.com` site and its API-key help page.

**What I left alone:**
- The `coinbase-pro` package has been deprecated since 2020. It still accepts the URIs you pass in, so the new hosts should work with it. I didn't swap it out.
- The code still signs requests with the key, secret and passphrase, and still calls `/profiles`, `/fees` and `/profiles/transfer`. I didn't confirm that the Exchange API accepts all three unchanged.
- Your existing Pro API keys may not work on Exchange. You may need to create new keys, and sandbox keys are separate from production ones.

Sources:
- [Coinbase Exchange Sandbox docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/introduction/sandbox.md)

handled.change: Coinbase Pro API retired; REST and WebSocket hosts (production and sandbox) moved to *.exchange.coinbase.com
handled.note: The host swap in the three strategy files is identical to A's. The README links point to slightly different doc paths, which is minor.

handled.change: Profile transfer response now includes transfer_id
handled.note: Only a logging change: the transfer result is now logged as JSON plus transfer_id. The original string concatenation would have printed [object Object], so this is harmless and marginally useful. No functional fix was needed. B doesn't say what changed in the API to require it.

breaks: Adds test_hosts.js, an ad-hoc static check at the repo root. It isn't wired into any test runner, and it asserts on a log string in buyAndSell.js.
The edited logger line in buyAndSell.js has an indentation off by one space.
B claims '10 changes' but explains almost none of them.

handled.change: Coinbase Pro API retired; REST and WebSocket hosts (production and sandbox) moved to *.exchange.coinbase.com
handled.note: All four URIs are swapped in all three strategy files. These constants feed both the SDK clients and the axios helper. The README docs links are updated. A is open about what it didn't verify: the production hosts, auth, and API key migration.

judge.why: Both make the same essential fix: replacing the Pro hosts with Exchange hosts everywhere they are used. B adds a cosmetic logging tweak and a brittle stray test file that no API change required, and its explanation is vague about the claimed changes. A makes the same substantive fix with less noise and clearly flags what it couldn't verify.
